literal: Lu Si, Yuan He, Liu Ni, Xue Ti
idiomatic: Lu Si, Yuan He, Liu Ni, and Xue Ti

literal: Lu Si; Yuan He's great-grandson Biao, great-great-grandson Shi, Shi's uncle Xiong; Liu Ni; Xue Ti
idiomatic: Lu Si; Yuan He — great-grandson Biao, great-great-grandson Shi, Shi's uncle Xiong; Liu Ni; Xue Ti

literal: Lu Si was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Lu Si was a native of Dai.

literal: His great-grandfather Gan and grandfather Yin for generations led their tribal division.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gan and grandfather Yin had led the tribe for generations.

literal: His father Tu, at the beginning of Emperor Daowu's reign, led his tribesmen on campaigns and repeatedly won merit; he held the posts of Warden of Lishi, Administrator of Shangdang, and Marquis Within the Passes.
idiomatic: His father Tu, in Daowu's early years, led the clansmen on campaign with repeated merit, rising to Warden of Lishi, Administrator of Shangdang, and Marquis Within the Passes.

literal: Si from youth was clever.
idiomatic: Si was clever from boyhood.

literal: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, Si inherited the title Marquis Within the Passes, served as Supervising Attendant, oversaw the Selection Bureau and Orchid Terrace affairs, and in office bent to no pressure.
idiomatic: When Mingyuan acceded, Si inherited the marquisate, became Supervising Attendant, ran selection and the Orchid Terrace, and would not be swayed in office.

literal: When Emperor Taiwu attacked Helian Chang, he ordered Si to command the garrison forces against the Rouran.
idiomatic: Taiwu's campaign against Helian Chang sent Si to command frontier troops against the Rouran.

literal: With Prince of Xiping Anqi he stormed Wulao; he was enfeoffed Duke of Jianye and appointed Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: With Prince Anqi of Xiping he took Wulao, was made Duke of Jianye, and became Governor of Ji.

literal: At the time the court graded provinces and commanderies; only Si and Qiu Chen, Administrator of Henei, ranked first in the realm.
idiomatic: When the realm was graded, only Si and Henei's Qiu Chen stood first.

literal: He was transferred to Grand General of the Wulao Garrison.
idiomatic: He became Grand General of the Wulao Garrison.

literal: When the Xiutu of Pingliang, Jin Ya, Qiang Di Ziyu, and others rebelled, he was again made Grand General of the Anding Garrison, pursued Ya and the rest, and captured them all.
idiomatic: Pingliang's Xiutu Jin Ya, the Qiang Di Ziyu, and others rebelled; he was shifted to Anding, pursued them, and took them all.

literal: He was moved to Grand General of the Huaihuang Garrison.
idiomatic: He was posted to Huaihuang as grand general.

literal: Before his term ended, the Gao-che mo-fu chieftains, fearing Si's severity, asked for the former warden Lang Gu.
idiomatic: Before his term ended, Gao-che mo-fu feared his harsh rule and asked for the former warden Lang Gu back.

literal: Taiwu granted it.
idiomatic: Taiwu agreed.

literal: Si was recalled; at court he said that within a year Gu alone would fail and the Gao-che would rebel.
idiomatic: Recalled to court, he said Gu would fail within a year and the Gao-che would rise.

literal: The emperor doubted the truth of it, rebuked him sharply, and sent him home with only his ducal title.
idiomatic: The emperor called it false, scolded him, and sent him home retaining only his rank.

literal: The next year the mo-fu indeed killed Gu and rebelled.
idiomatic: Next year the mo-fu killed Gu and rebelled, as he had said.

literal: The emperor was greatly startled and summoned Si to ask the reason.
idiomatic: The emperor was stunned and summoned Si to explain.

literal: Si said: "The custom of the Gao-che sets no ritual between high and low; men without ritual are hard to rule from above.
idiomatic: Si said, "Gao-che custom knows no ritual between high and low; the unruly are hard to govern.

literal: Your servant governed with stern authority and bound them with law, wishing gradually to train and guide them so they would know their limits.
idiomatic: I ruled with stern law, hoping to teach them their bounds.

literal: But those who hate the upright and despise integrity are many; therefore they sued me as loveless and praised Gu's kindness.
idiomatic: Many hate the upright; they called me harsh and praised Gu.

literal: When Gu returned to command, delighted at his fame, he was sure to heap favor on the people, mock me as wrong, and aim to win them only by leniency and forbearance.
idiomatic: Gu back in command would favor the people, mock my severity, and rule by indulgence alone.

literal: Men without ritual easily grow insolent; within a year high and low would vanish.
idiomatic: Without ritual, insolence spreads; within a year rank would collapse.

literal: Once rank was gone, then to restrain them by force would fill men with resentment.
idiomatic: Then force would breed deep resentment.

literal: When resentment is many, defeat and disorder stand plain."
idiomatic: Much resentment means open revolt."

literal: The emperor sighed: "Your body is short—how long your foresight!"
idiomatic: The emperor sighed, "Short in stature, long in foresight!"

literal: That same day he was again appointed Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: That day he was reappointed Regular Attendant.

literal: On the emperor's Rouran campaign and the conquest of Liangzhou, he often followed the train and separately directed baggage trains.
idiomatic: On the Rouran campaign and the fall of Liangzhou he followed the train and directed baggage.

literal: Again with Prince of Gaoliang Na he crossed south of the Yellow River to raid territory.
idiomatic: Again with Prince Na of Gaoliang he crossed the Yellow River to raid.

literal: He was then made Grand General of the Chang'an Garrison.
idiomatic: He was made Grand General of Chang'an.

literal: With Prince Na he struck Gai Wu at Xingcheng and captured Wu's two uncles.
idiomatic: With Prince Na he fought Gai Wu at Xingcheng and took Wu's two uncles.

literal: The generals wished to send them to the capital; Si alone refused, saying: "If Wu is not beheaded, Chang'an's troubles may not end.
idiomatic: The generals wanted them sent to the capital; Si refused: "Unless Wu dies, Chang'an may not rest.

literal: One man in hiding—who but his intimates can seize him?
idiomatic: One fugitive—only intimates can catch him.

literal: To halt a hundred thousand men to chase one man is not the best plan.
idiomatic: Halting an army of a hundred thousand for one man is poor strategy.

literal: Better secretly promise Wu's uncles freedom for their wives and children and let them hunt Wu themselves."
idiomatic: Better promise the uncles their families and let them hunt Wu."

literal: The generals all said: "Now we have his two uncles; Wu is alone—what could he still do?"
idiomatic: They said, "We hold both uncles; Wu is alone—what can he do?"

literal: Si said: "Have you never seen a venomous snake?
idiomatic: Si said, "Have you never seen a viper?"

literal: If you do not cut off its head, it can still harm.
idiomatic: Uncut, its head still kills.

literal: How, when removing a disease of the heart, can you say its kind must be left—can that be right?"
idiomatic: When excising a heart's disease, who leaves the brood?"

literal: He therefore released Wu's two uncles and set a deadline with them.
idiomatic: He released the uncles and set a date.

literal: When the day came the uncles did not appear; the generals all blamed Si.
idiomatic: The day passed without them; all blamed Si.

literal: Si said: "They have not yet found their chance; they will not break faith."
idiomatic: Si said, "They lack opportunity; they will not betray us."

literal: Days later Wu was indeed beheaded and brought in—everything as he had said.
idiomatic: Days later Wu's head arrived—exactly as he foretold.

literal: Si's clear strategy and solitary decisions were all of this kind.
idiomatic: Si's foresight and solitary resolve were always thus.

literal: He was moved to Grand Director of the Inner Court.
idiomatic: He became Grand Director of the Inner Court.

literal: When Liu Chao and others of Anding's Lushui rebelled, Taiwu, because Si's authority and kindness extended through Guanzhong, ordered him in his existing office additionally to be Area Commander of Qin and Yong forces, garrisoning Chang'an.
idiomatic: Liu Chao of Lushui rebelled in Anding; Taiwu, knowing Si's name in Guanzhong, made him Area Commander of Qin and Yong while keeping his post at Chang'an.

literal: The emperor said: "Chao and the rest rely on terrain and disobey the royal command. If I give you a heavy force, Chao will surely unite with them;
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Chao holds the passes; a heavy force unites them;

literal: if I give you a light force, you cannot control them.
idiomatic: a light force cannot hold them.

literal: Now I send you to settle them by strategy."
idiomatic: Go settle them by stratagem."

literal: Si therefore rode alone to his post.
idiomatic: Si rode alone to command.

literal: On arrival he proclaimed authority and showed success and failure; Chao still had no mind to submit.
idiomatic: He proclaimed majesty and showed outcomes; Chao would not yield.

literal: Si then led his personal guard to see Chao.
idiomatic: Si led his guard to call on Chao.

literal: Chao sent word ahead: "Beyond three hundred men, bow and horse are the greeting;
idiomatic: Chao warned, "Past three hundred, expect bows;

literal: within three hundred, wine and food will be provided."
idiomatic: within three hundred, wine and meat."

literal: He therefore took two hundred horsemen to Chao.
idiomatic: He took two hundred riders to Chao.

literal: Chao's guard was very strict; they drank until all were drunk and returned.
idiomatic: Chao's guard was tight; they drank to drunkenness and left.

literal: Later, feigning a hunt, he went to Chao.
idiomatic: Later he feigned a hunt and visited Chao.

literal: He agreed with his soldiers: "When we strike today, drunkenness is the signal."
idiomatic: He told his men, "When we move, feign drunkenness."

literal: Si then pretended drunkenness, mounted, shouted, and beheaded Chao.
idiomatic: Si played drunk, mounted, shouted, and struck off Chao's head.

literal: The soldiers answered with a shout and charged; the rebellion was pacified.
idiomatic: His men charged at once; the rebellion ended.

literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and summoned him as Grand Director of the Outer Court.
idiomatic: The emperor rejoiced and made him Grand Director of the Outer Court.

literal: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne, because his son Li had merit in settling the succession, Si was advanced to Prince of Dongping.
idiomatic: Wencheng's accession, with son Li's merit in the succession, raised Si to Prince of Dongping.

literal: He died at sixty-seven; posthumous name Prince Cheng.
idiomatic: He died at sixty-seven, posthumous name Cheng.

literal: He had twelve sons.
idiomatic: He had twelve sons.

literal: The eldest, Xu, was very clever and had his father's manner.
idiomatic: Eldest son Xu was clever and like his father.

literal: Wencheng saw him and was pleased, telling the court: "I often sighed that his father's wisdom exceeded his frame—this one surpasses his father!"
idiomatic: Wencheng met him and said, "His father's mind outgrew his body—this boy outgrows his father!"

literal: In youth he was Junior Grand Master of the Inner Court.
idiomatic: As a youth he served as Junior Grand Master of the Inner Court.

literal: Serving superiors and receiving subordinates, in conduct and gift he could always anticipate others' wishes.
idiomatic: Up and down the ranks he anticipated every wish in bearing and gift.

literal: None who worked with him failed to love him.
idiomatic: All who served with him loved him.

literal: At the beginning of Xing'an he was enfeoffed Marquis of Liaocheng.
idiomatic: At Xing'an's start he was made Marquis of Liaocheng.

literal: Sent out as Governor of Xiang Province, with acting title Prince of Changguang.
idiomatic: He went out as Governor of Xiang, acting Prince of Changguang.

literal: His government was clear and level; he curbed the strong and aided the weak.
idiomatic: He ruled plainly, curbing the strong and helping the weak.

literal: In the province were venerable elders of long-standing virtue and fame; he treated them with the rites due friends.
idiomatic: He honored aged men of local renown as friends.

literal: He questioned them on administration and charged them with strategy; there were ten such men, called the Ten Worthies.
idiomatic: Ten such elders he called the Ten Worthies and charged with counsel.

literal: He also selected more than a hundred strong-house sons from the counties as his foster sons.
idiomatic: He took over a hundred strong-house sons as foster sons.

literal: He received them warmly, gave them clothes, and sent each home as his eyes and ears.
idiomatic: He clothed them and sent them home as informants.

literal: Thus hidden wrongdoing was exposed; nothing failed to prove true.
idiomatic: Hidden crime surfaced; nothing failed to check.

literal: The people thought him divine; none dared rob or steal.
idiomatic: The people called him divine; robbery ceased.

literal: Seven years in the province, his household remained utterly poor.
idiomatic: Seven years in office, his house stayed poor.

literal: Summoned as Regular Attendant, more than a thousand people begged to keep Xu.
idiomatic: Recalled as Regular Attendant, over a thousand petitioned to keep him.

literal: Emperor Xianwen would not agree and told the ministers: "Xu's good government—what ancient could add to it?"
idiomatic: Xianwen refused and told the court, "What ancient surpassed Xu's rule?"

literal: He granted five hundred bolts of silk and ten slaves and concubines.
idiomatic: He gave five hundred bolts of silk and ten slaves.

literal: When Xu left office, clerks and people heaped cloth and silk to give him.
idiomatic: On his departure clerks and people piled gifts of cloth.

literal: Xu accepted none; the people would not take their gifts back either, and with that cloth they raised a Buddhist temple, hence named the Temple of Prince Changguang.
idiomatic: He refused all; the people built a temple from the cloth, the Temple of Prince Changguang.

literal: Later he inherited his father's title and was changed to Prince of Jian'an.
idiomatic: He later inherited and was made Prince of Jian'an.

literal: Xiu, styled Bolin, was Xu's fifth son.
idiomatic: Xiu, styled Bolin, was Xu's fifth son.

literal: His mother, of the Helian clan, stood seven chi nine cun tall and had great wifely virtue.
idiomatic: His mother Helian stood seven chi nine cun and was deeply virtuous.

literal: Xu intended to pass the title to Xiu.
idiomatic: Xu meant the title for Xiu.

literal: When Xiu was nine, Xu told him: "Your grandfather the Prince of Dongping had twelve sons; I am the eldest legitimate son and inherited the house.
idiomatic: At nine Xiu heard, "Your grandfather had twelve sons; I am eldest and heir.

literal: Now I am old and leave you still young—can you bear to be head of the Lu clan?"
idiomatic: I am old and you a child—can you head the house?"

literal: Xiu answered: "If it is not a contest of strength, why fear being young!"
idiomatic: Xiu said, "If it is not wrestling, why fear youth?"

literal: Xu marveled and made Xiu his heir.
idiomatic: Xu marveled and named him heir.

literal: When Xu died, Xiu inherited the title.
idiomatic: Xiu inherited on Xu's death.

literal: Xiu was deep, steady, and sparing of words; he loved reading.
idiomatic: Xiu was grave, quiet, and fond of books.

literal: As a meritorious minister's descendant he was Chief of the Imperial Guard, then rose to Minister of the Imperial Clan and Grand Rectifier of Si Province.
idiomatic: A minister's son, he became Chief of the Imperial Guard, then Minister of the Imperial Clan and Grand Rectifier of Si.

literal: When his cousin Rui's affair broke out, he was dismissed.
idiomatic: Cousin Rui's scandal cost him his post.

literal: At the beginning of Jingming he was tried as Administrator of Henei.
idiomatic: In Jingming he tried governing Henei.

literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi rebelled and sent his son Tanhe and others first to seize Henei.
idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang rebelled and sent son Tanhe to seize Henei.

literal: Hearing of Xi's revolt, Xiu beheaded Tanhe.
idiomatic: Hearing of the revolt, Xiu beheaded Tanhe.
